headline: Microsoft's Decision-1 model, built on Alibaba's open Qwen3.5-9B, scores options with probabilities and has been used inside Microsoft to match OpenAI models at much higher speed and lower cost, on Microsoft's own tests.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: Microsoft launched the model about 9 Oct 2026 and our 10 Oct edition carried it; ForkLog adds only Microsoft's own internal examples.
importance_line: Companies that run many automated checks could pay far less per decision, and the choice of a Chinese company's open model as the base shows a US tech giant building on it, but every speed, cost and accuracy figure is Microsoft's own.
summary: ForkLog reports, citing Microsoft, that Microsoft-Decision-1, which our 10 Oct 2026 edition reported at launch, was made by further training Alibaba's open Qwen3.5-9B model to give a probability for each option in a fixed list, such as yes or no, instead of writing text. New since that edition are Microsoft's internal examples: its Xbox Research team labelled more than 10,000 reviews gathered from surveys, Steam and X at quality it calls comparable to GPT-6 Sol, over 14 times faster and at 200 times lower cost, and the Copilot team matched GPT-5.6 Luna in grading chatbot answers at a hundred times the speed.
notes: Follow-up of the 10 Oct 2026 entry. Read ForkLog in full; Microsoft's own post was not opened.
